meeting.title: Ashby embedded analytics working session
meeting.summary: Technical working session on Ashby's semantic layer. The group walked through the metrics block syntax in dbt and agreed the first tranche of metrics for the embedded dashboards. Bram committed to having the first ten metric definitions in the dbt .yml by Wednesday June 17th. Naming convention agreed: snake_case with a domain prefix.
action_items: Bram to define the first ten metrics in the dbt .yml by Wednesday June 17th
key_decisions: Metric naming convention: snake_case with a domain prefix (e.g. recruiting_offer_acceptance_rate)
First tranche is the ten metrics needed by the embedded customer dashboards, not internal reporting
meeting.notes: Screen-shared through fct_applications.yml as the worked example. Bram was comfortable with the syntax by the end of the session.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Today is hands-on: we'll walk the metrics block syntax together and agree which metrics come first.

transcript.speaker: Bram Peeters
transcript.text: Perfect. I've got fct_applications open — can we use that as the worked example?

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Yes, ideal. So under the model you add a metrics block — label, type, then the expression. Let's write offer acceptance rate together.

transcript.speaker: Bram Peeters
transcript.text: Okay… type ratio, numerator is offers accepted, denominator is total offers extended. Like this?

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Exactly like that. Run dbt parse and you'll see it compile. That's the whole workflow — metrics as code, reviewed in your normal PR flow.

transcript.speaker: Lotte Janssens
transcript.text: Nice. On priorities — the embedded dashboards for customers need about ten metrics. I'd say those come before anything for internal reporting.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Agreed, embedded first. That's time to hire, offer acceptance rate, and the rest of the list from the discovery doc?

transcript.speaker: Lotte Janssens
transcript.text: That list, yes. Ten metrics, all off fct_applications and fct_interviews.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: One thing to settle before you write them: naming. We recommend snake_case with a domain prefix so autocomplete groups them.

transcript.speaker: Bram Peeters
transcript.text: Works for me — recruiting_offer_acceptance_rate, pipeline_time_to_hire, that style. Let's lock that in.

transcript.speaker: Lotte Janssens
transcript.text: Locked. Bram, how long do you need for the first ten?

transcript.speaker: Bram Peeters
transcript.text: Now that I've seen the syntax, not long. I'll have the first ten metric definitions in the dbt yml by Wednesday the 17th — time to hire, offer acceptance rate, the ones we listed.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Wednesday the 17th is great. Once they compile, they show up in Quarry automatically — no extra step on our side.

transcript.speaker: Bram Peeters
transcript.text: Even better. I'll tag you on the PR so you can sanity-check the expressions.

transcript.speaker: Ines Ferreira
transcript.text: Please do. Good session — same time next week to review them live.
